rr.intro1.text: Ripple lives in the kelp beside a bright coral reef.

rr.intro2.text: But after a very hot summer, part of the reef turned white.

rr.intro3.text: The coral isn't gone. It's weak, and it needs help to recover.

rr.intro4.text: Let's learn how the reef works and help it bloom again!

rr.between2.text: Look! The fish are coming back to the reef.

rr.between4.text: Corals have tiny partners living inside them.

rr.between6.text: Every step you take brings more colour back to the reef.

rr.outro1.text: The reef is full of colour again!

rr.outro2.text: You learned how the reef works and chose ways to help.

rr.ready.text: Let's look closely and help the reef bloom again!

rr.back.text: Welcome back to the reef! Ready to help?

rr.prompt.tutorial.text: Drag the parrotfish to the food it eats.

rr.prompt.home.text: Put each one where it gets what it needs.

rr.prompt.chain.text: Build the food chain, starting with the sun.

rr.prompt.partner.text: What do the tiny algae give the coral?

rr.prompt.gives.text: What does the coral give its tiny algae?

rr.prompt.light.text: Why does reef coral grow in clear, shallow water?

rr.prompt.bleach.text: Put the story of the white coral in order.

rr.prompt.recover.text: Put the story of the coral's recovery in order.

rr.prompt.sort.text: Does each one help the reef or harm it?

rr.prompt.grazers.text: Algae is covering this coral. Which animals keep the algae in check?

rr.prompt.plant.text: Plant the coral pieces where they'll grow best.

rr.prompt.chart.text: When was the reef most at risk?

rr.prompt.count.text: How many weeks was the water above the dashed line?

rr.help.eats.text: Look at its mouth. Grazers nibble plants and algae. Hunters catch fish.

rr.help.home.text: Living things need the right home: sunlight, the right ground, or a place to hide.

rr.help.chain.text: Arrows show where the energy goes: from the food to the eater.

rr.help.sun.text: Every food chain starts with the sun. Algae and seagrass use sunlight to make food.

rr.help.coral.text: Coral is an animal! Tiny algae live inside it and share the food they make.

rr.help.bleach.text: When water stays too warm, coral pushes out its algae and turns white. If the water cools, it can recover.

rr.help.chem.text: Coral bleaching isn't caused by bleach. It happens when the water stays too warm.

rr.help.recover.text: When the water cools, the tiny algae can move back into the coral.

rr.help.sort.text: Ask: does it keep the water clean and cool, and keep plenty of grazers?

rr.help.grazers.text: Fish and urchins that eat algae keep it from covering the coral.

rr.help.plant.text: New coral needs sunlight and a clean, steady place to grow.

rr.help.chart.text: Look for weeks above the dashed line. Many warm weeks in a row are the hardest for coral.

rr.help.count.text: Count only the bars that rise above the dashed line.

rr.hint.shark.text: Reef sharks hunt fish. They don't eat algae or seagrass.

rr.hint.hottest.text: That was the hottest week, but it was short. Find the longest warm spell.

rr.praise.2.text: Yes, coral is an animal with tiny partners.

rr.praise.3.text: You chose actions that really help.

rr.praise.eats.text: You matched the animal to its food!

rr.praise.home.text: You checked what each one needs!

rr.praise.bleach.text: You followed the story, step by step!

rr.praise.plant.text: You checked every spot for light and a steady base!

rr.idle.text: Move a card into place, then press Check.
